metadata.description:
Frozen benchmark, partitioning protocols, baselines, stored predictions and analysis code accompanying the manuscript TCR-IMAP: A Dual-Encoder Cross-Attention Model for TCR–MHC Platform Contact Map Prediction.

What TCR-IMAP does. It predicts which residues of a T-cell receptor contact which residues of the MHC class I α1/α2 platform, from amino-acid sequence alone: two Transformer encoders represent the TCR and MHC residues, cross-attention couples them, and a bilinear head returns a probability for every candidate residue pair. The archive ships the model together with the apparatus it was measured with: 174 curated TCR–peptide–MHC class I complexes, all with a human MHC class I heavy chain, collapsing to 69 TCR clusters at a similarity ratio of 0.70; contact labels and candidate masks over a 174 × 75 × 84 tensor holding 893,928 resolved residue pairs of which 5,281 (0.59 %) are contacts at a 4.5 Å heavy-atom threshold, keyed by IMGT number together with insertion code; five partitioning protocols fixed before the reported results were produced, with a declared primary metric, protocol and comparison; within-fold pair-frequency priors; complete stored pairwise predictions for all five protocols; per-complex per-residue metrics; comparator reimplementations with a full provenance and deviation table; a training-size-matched control whose plan was committed before any downsampled model was trained; the authoritative identity-threshold sweep at 20,000 cluster-bootstrap resamples; and the molecular-dynamics analysis code with its twelve output tables.

A worked example reproduces the reported pairwise results from the stored arrays on a CPU in under a minute. Retraining is optional and needs a GPU.

Scope and limitations. Paired αβ TCRs on human MHC class I, α1/α2 platform; receptors are human in 165 complexes, mouse in 8 and mixed chimpanzee/human α in 1. MHC class II, γδ receptors and non-human MHC are out of scope. The archive contains no sequence-to-input builder: applying the model outside the cohort requires an IMGT numbering step that is documented but not implemented. The predeclared primary comparison is unresolved at this sample size (+0.0312 [−0.0049, +0.0650], p = 0.088) and is reported as it stands. The canonical-CDR-only sensitivity covers 14 comparisons but not that primary comparison, because the per-residue benchmark stores metrics rather than predictions and writes no checkpoint; no historical per-residue checkpoint or prediction array exists. Molecular-dynamics trajectories are not included. Source structures are from STCRDab and the Protein Data Bank. Four cleaned MD-input coordinate files (3VXS, 5YXN, 7N1F and 8EO8) are included; other source coordinates are referenced through retrieval instructions.

Funding and acknowledgments. D.W. is supported by the National Key R&D Program of China (2024YFA1306400 and 2023YFE0199200), the National Natural Science Foundation of China (32570803 and 32030063), and the Intergovernmental International Scientific and Technological Innovation Cooperation Program. The computations were performed in part at Pengcheng Laboratory and the Center for High-Performance Computing, Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
